articles.title: Extended reality takes visitors from the ruins of West Bank to 17th-century Amsterdam at Venice Immersive
articles.summary: From frivolous to serious, virtual nosy passersby to the impact of climate change, the groundbreaking festival draws to a close – but this year the exhibits live on. The first installation one encounters on visiting Venice Immersive, the film festival’s reliably head-spinning showcase for new…
body: The passerby is not real – or rather, he’s only real in the box. He wears a blue suit and speaks with a heavy French accent and tells a tale that would sit badly in polite company. He says that I must have too much time on my hands, to stand hunched over this eyepiece for several minutes on end. “Why do people keep looking inside this box?” he demands. “What is it that they hope to see? It is not reality.”

The name of Celine Daemen’s fabulous installation – Nothing to See Here – is immediately belied by the presence of 67 further exhibits (the organisers refer to them as “experiences”) arranged cheek by jowl on a small dedicated island. But the creepy Frenchman’s contention should not be so lightly brushed aside. Venice Immersive’s projects run the gamut from the frivolous to the serious, the escapist to the harrowing. But is the island a backwater or a new-found land? Does it represent reality or different versions of a dream?

articles.title: Gary Oldman Predicts HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ Series Will Be ‘More Satisfying’ for Fans Than the Movies
articles.summary: Gary Oldman, who played Sirius Black in four “Harry Potter” movies, said he believes HBO’s forthcoming TV series adaptation set in the Wizarding World will be a bigger crowd-pleaser than the Warner Bros. films. That’s because the movies were significantly abridged from J.K.
body: Oldman has previously opined that Sirius Black, a character he loves, did not get enough screen time in the movies. “He wasn’t in it enough. He turned up and then he went through the veil,” Oldman told IndieWire in 2024. Oldman’s Black first appeared in 2004’s “Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban,” but he had only cameos in “Goblet of Fire” and “Deathly Hallows Part 2″ and a brief appearance in “Order of the Phoenix” before his character is killed off.
That said, Oldman told EW he is “proud” and “grateful” to have been part of the “Harry Potter” films “because it is such a phenomenon, the like of which I don’t think you’re ever gonna see again.”

“When you think of that initial cast, someone in the story who doesn’t get a lot of credit anymore is [director] Chris Columbus, who set the world up and cast it,” he said. “We were extraordinarily lucky to have those people come back again, and again, and again, and literally grow into those roles.”
Oldman will next appear in Season 6 of Apple TV’s “Slow Horses,” which premieres Sept. 16.

articles.title: Paramount Argues States’ Antitrust Suit Will ‘Collapse Under Scrutiny’
articles.summary: Paramount’s lawyers filed a legal response to the states’ antitrust lawsuit against the Warner Bros. Discovery merger on Friday, sketching out arguments and defenses it may use at a trial next March.
body: “Day by day, the weak case against this Merger gets even weaker,” the company argued, adding that it also plans to challenge the states’ market definitions. “Plaintiffs’ case amounts to a series of attempted shortcuts and assumptions that collapse under scrutiny.”

California led the state coalition in suing to block the merger in July, arguing that the deal will create unlawful concentration in the basic cable market and in the wide-release and blockbuster theatrical markets. The DOJ had earlier approved the merger, issuing a memo laying out its reasoning for why the deal should be allowed to go forward.
States typically work with the DOJ in antitrust cases, but under the Trump administration California and several others have often charted their own course.
Paramount has repeatedly argued that the deal will be pro-competitive, and will result in more movies and TV shows.

articles.summary: In "The Julia Set," she portrays a numbers genius in the most convincing way possible — by wearing her virtuosity lightly and casually, as if it were second nature (which, for someone like Julia, it is).
body: She plays a math prodigy who falls into an affair with her dream-preppie TA. An unwise idea, but the movie plays it out with startling conviction.

There are two major pieces of news to come out of “ The Julia Set,” the nothing-short-of-terrific new movie that premiered tonight at the Toronto Film Festival. It’s the first movie to feature Chase Infiniti since her breakout role as the Leonardo DiCaprio character’s daughter in “One Battle After Another,” and the first piece of news is that it confirms her movie-star mettle and astonishing quality of lyrical wised-up innocence as an actor.

articles.title: Faith review – intense performances power startling and unsettling tale of mysterious suitor
articles.summary: Toronto film festival: Erin Doherty plays a happily single mother in a downbeat town courted by an enigmatic James McAvoy in this expertly taut drama. Erin Doherty and James McAvoy both bring their A-game in this startling, involving movie from British writer-director Paul Andrew Williams, whose…
body: We are in a downbeat British town, perhaps somewhere in the London estuary, a place to which a candy factory provides employment. Mina (played by Doherty) is a smart, capable single mum to 9-year-old Jamie (Smylie Bradwell); she works on the production line in cap and hairnet like all the others: much liked by everyone there. She is not fussed by the absence of Jamie’s dad and is perfectly content with hanging out with her friends and her sister (Liv Hill).

Williams shrewdly controls the film’s growing, complex mood: a cocktail of dread, fascination and something else, as if Mina has been made a party to some occult conspiracy that Michael isn’t in any hurry to reveal. He already seems to know something about Mina’s babysitter that Mina herself hasn’t suspected. The film’s central dramatic events then kick the mood up into a higher gear. Mina is passionate, bewildered and Michael assumes the priestly air of someone who has seen it all before and who is either here to help or is some kind of vampiric outsider. The problem seemed initially to be that he was too good to be true. Clearly that isn’t the issue.
points: Toronto film festival: Erin Doherty plays a happily single mother in a downbeat town courted by an enigmatic James McAvoy in this expertly taut drama.

articles.title: River review – so-so survival slasher offers more of the same and little else
articles.summary: Toronto film festival: strong performances from two experienced scream queens and some surprisingly thoughtful direction can’t elevate yet another stalk-by-numbers horror.
body: I t would be unwise and unfair to expect that Toronto’s genre-led Midnight Madness strand would open with quite the same jolt as it did last year with the record-breaking horror hit Obsession. That film was an outlier in almost every respect, both as it premiered and as it was unleashed on wider crowds, the highest-grossing festival acquisition of all time topping out at over $513m worldwide and sparking genuine Oscar buzz.

articles.title: The Housewife review – Naomi Watts is a secret suburban Nazi in an overcooked melodrama
articles.summary: Toronto film festival: the chilling true story of a woman who tried to hide from her wartime crimes gets turned into a strangely inert misfire. The first scene of the 60s-set drama The Housewife is a closeup of a whistling kettle, an early “wink, wink” sign that we’re watching a story where…
body: Perhaps if it had been pitched closer to its adjacently named cousin The Housemaid, as a silly, sensationalist thriller, such heavy-handed decision-making would feel more well-suited. But instead, while some scenes flirt with the idea of something juicier, this is a stuffy and stodgy slab of self-serious, old-school Oscar bait complete with all the shouting, crying, throwing and finger-pointing one would expect. Think overcooked rather than slow simmer.

Strangely handled like a big first-act twist, by ensuring that we don’t hear the husband’s American accent for a convenient while and hoping we don’t spot the very clear signposting, we discover that Hermine is the Nazi and has been stringing Joseph along. She claims that her job was a mere nurse, saving rather than slaughtering, and that by associating her with misdeeds, Joseph is showing his ignorance of what the Holocaust was like to live through (“You do not know war in America,” she tells him). But a story is a story and, in Joseph’s mind, a Nazi is a Nazi especially when he finds new information on what really happened.
points: Toronto film festival: the chilling true story of a woman who tried to hide from her wartime crimes gets turned into a strangely inert misfire.

articles.title: Sorry, Caleb Hearon Is Not Your Clown in ‘Trash Mountain’ Grief Dramedy
articles.summary: The comic and actor and co-star Zooey Deschanel helped unveil Kris Rey’s indie about love and death penned by Hearon and Ruby Caster during a world premiere at the Toronto Film Festival.
body: So when the comic and actor co-wrote Trash Mountain with Ruby Caster, Hearon had to consider how much to lean into comedy as tears roll down his cheeks while starring alongside Zooey Deschenal in Kris Rey’s dramedy about love and grief.

Caster told the Scotiabank audience she was wary with Hearon as a skilled comedian in writing the wrong joke that crossed a line between drawing laughter and tears around grief. That led Hearon to break the tension by joking: “You stepped across a lot of lines. And I want to talk about that, here, tonight.”

In Trash Mountain, Hearon plays Gavin, a young gay Chicago man forced back home to rural Missouri after his hoarder father died. Once there, Gavin, who appears to have walked away from everyone he has ever loved in life, has an emotional reunion with his half-sister Abbi, played by Deschanel.

“This was a really complicated guy, and he didn’t have a perfect son either,” Hearon said of his real-life father whose inspired character doesn’t appear onscreen in Trash Mountain. But the late father is ever-present as Gavin and Abbi pick through the detritus of his life and which grows in the front yard of his home as a mountain of rubbish to be hauled away.

articles.title: 'Ted Lasso' Season 4 Officially Rewrites the Show's Most Controversial Storyline
articles.summary: With its return for Season 4, Ted Lasso officially rewrites one of the show's most controversial storylines, giving it more nuance and depth.
body: Editor's note: The below contains spoilers for Ted Lasso Season 4 Episode 6.

Ted Lasso Season 4 is taking the beloved Apple TV series in a different direction with a focus on the journey of AFC Richmond's women's team. While some storylines have carried over from previous seasons, like Keeley ( Juno Temple ) and Roy's ( Brett Goldstein ) on-again, off-again romance, Season 4's latest episode, "Don't Jump Around Much Anymore," shines a spotlight on a different character with a personal connection to the show's titular character, Jason Sudeikis.

Ted's ex-wife, Michelle ( Andrea Anders ), initially becomes an antagonist of sorts, given that her and Ted's separation and eventual divorce impact Ted's storyline — but that is never more true than in Season 3, when Michelle's new boyfriend and former therapist, Dr. Jacob ( Mike O'Gorman ), is introduced. The unethical nature of their relationship bothered many fans, but Season 4 offers a new perspective on these events, revealing them as more complex than Ted, or the audience, realized.
points: With its return for Season 4, Ted Lasso officially rewrites one of the show's most controversial storylines, giving it more nuance and depth.

articles.title: Sydney Sweeney Faces Backlash for Sexualized Novig Ad: “Exactly Why Women in Sports Aren’t Taken Seriously”
articles.summary: Many online users, including women who work in the sports industry, have shared their frustration with the actress' campaign for the sports trading app, which features multiple shots of her mostly naked body covered with different sports balls and uniforms.
body: More than a year after her American Eagle ad controversy, Sydney Sweeney is facing backlash for another campaign: her sexualized promotion for sports trading app Novig.

The Euphoria actress partnered up with Novig on Wednesday to support the new platform, which launched last month. She not only starred in the ad but also joined Novig as a strategic partner and equity holder.

Some users are arguing Sweeney’s ad for the age-restricted platform could have used an R-rated rating as well. “I couldn’t believe when that ad came on the tv. I had my 2 children in the living room I had to yell at them to look away from the TV. I don’t understand WHY they would need to create such a [vulgar] ad,” a TikTok user commented on a post made by Marissa Womack, manager of game day promotions and programming for minor league baseball team the Harrisburg Senators.
